get_session_info.title: Get the API session
get_session_info.description: Read the current API session -- which organization and user it belongs to, and when it expires. The cheapest call that proves the session is still good.

output.description: The session's organization, user and expiry.

list_organizations.title: List login organizations
list_organizations.description: Read the BILL organizations this login can sign in to, with their ids. An organization id is part of the login exchange, so this is how you learn which one to use.

page.description: Page cursor from a previous response.

output.description: The organizations available to the login.

list_vendors.title: List vendors
list_vendors.description: Read the organization's vendors -- the people and companies you pay. `filters` takes BILL's filter syntax, e.g. "isActive:true", and ids come back prefixed with `009`.

page.description: Page cursor from a previous response.

filters.description: Filter expression in BILL's syntax, e.g. "isActive:true".

get_vendor.title: Get a vendor
get_vendor.description: Read one vendor by its `009...` id -- name, address, payment details and tax settings.

vendor_id.description: The vendor's id, which begins with `009`.

create_vendor.title: Create a vendor
create_vendor.description: Create a vendor. `address` is required and must be a real postal address, since BILL may post them a cheque. `payment_information` sets how they are paid -- including bank details, which turn on electronic payment -- and `additional_info` carries the tax id and 1099 flag the IRS needs.

short_name.description: Short name, used where space is tight.

account_number.description: Your account number with this vendor; printed on payments.

payment_information.description: How the vendor is paid -- {"payeeName": ..., "email": ..., "bankAccount": {"accountNumber": ..., "routingNumber": ...}}. Sending bank details enables electronic payment.

bill_currency.description: Currency their bills are denominated in.

output.description: The created vendor, with its `009...` id.

update_vendor.title: Update a vendor
update_vendor.description: Change a vendor's details. Only the fields you send are touched -- including inside `address` and `payment_information`, which are merged rather than replaced wholesale.

account_number.description: New account number with the vendor.

additional_info.description: Tax or terms fields to change.

archive_vendor.title: Archive a vendor
archive_vendor.description: Archive a vendor so they can no longer be chosen on new bills. Their history stays; restore_vendor brings them back.

restore_vendor.title: Restore an archived vendor
restore_vendor.description: Bring an archived vendor back into use on new bills and payments.

get_vendor_bank_account.title: Get a vendor's bank account
get_vendor_bank_account.description: Read the bank account BILL holds for a vendor, in the masked form the API returns. Whether one exists decides if they can be paid electronically.

output.description: The vendor's bank account details, masked.

get_vendor_payment_options.title: Get a vendor's payment options
get_vendor_payment_options.description: Read how this vendor can actually be paid for a given amount -- ACH, cheque, virtual card, international -- which is what `funding_account.type` on a payment must agree with. The amount matters, because some methods have limits.

amount.description: The amount you intend to pay them.

output.description: The payment methods available for that vendor and amount.

list_bills.title: List bills
list_bills.description: Read the bills you owe. `filters` in BILL's syntax is how you get a work queue -- unpaid bills, bills for one vendor, bills due before a date. Ids come back prefixed with `00n`.

page.description: Page cursor from a previous response.

filters.description: Filter expression in BILL's syntax, e.g. "vendorId:009...".

get_bill.title: Get a bill
get_bill.description: Read one bill by its `00n...` id -- vendor, due date, line items, classifications and approval state.

bill_id.description: The bill's id, which begins with `00n`.

create_bill.title: Create a bill
create_bill.description: Record a bill you owe a vendor. `invoice` carries *their* invoice number and date, `line_items` the amounts, and `due_date` when it must be paid. Creating the bill does not pay it -- approval and then a payment do. Set `allow_duplicate_invoice_number` to false to have BILL reject a repeat of an invoice number you already have.

vendor_id.description: The vendor charging you, by their `009...` id.

due_date.description: When the bill must be paid, as YYYY-MM-DD.

invoice.description: The vendor's invoice -- {"invoiceNumber": ..., "invoiceDate": "YYYY-MM-DD"}. Both are required.

line_items.description: What the bill is for, each {"amount": ..., optionally "quantity", "price", "description" and "classifications"}.

payment_term_id.description: Payment term id, which drives the due date in your accounting.

pay_from_chart_of_account_id.description: Chart of accounts id the payment should be booked against.

purchase_order_number.description: Purchase order this bill relates to.

include_approvals.description: Have BILL return the bill's approval information in the response.

allow_duplicate_invoice_number.description: Set false to reject the bill when its invoice number already exists for this vendor -- the duplicate-payment guard.

output.description: The created bill, with its `00n...` id.

create_bills_bulk.title: Create many bills at once
create_bills_bulk.description: Create a batch of bills in one call, each shaped like create_bill's body. The import path for a month of vendor invoices.

bills.description: The bills to create, each shaped like create_bill's body.

output.description: The created bills, with any per-bill errors.

update_bill.title: Update a bill
update_bill.description: Change a bill. `line_items` entries must each carry their own `id` -- omit an existing line and it is removed, so read the bill first. `policy_rematch` decides whether BILL re-runs its approval policy against the changed bill.

vendor_id.description: Move the bill to another vendor.

line_items.description: The bill's line items after the update, each with its `id`. Lines you leave out are removed.

policy_rematch.description: Re-run the approval policy against the changed bill.

archive_bill.title: Archive a bill
archive_bill.description: Archive a bill so it drops out of the payable queue. It is not deleted and restore_bill undoes this -- but archiving a bill that has a payment against it is not the way to reverse the payment.

restore_bill.title: Restore an archived bill
restore_bill.description: Bring an archived bill back into the payable queue.

list_bills_pending_approval.title: List bills waiting for my approval
list_bills_pending_approval.description: Read the bills awaiting approval from the user this session belongs to -- the approver's inbox, and what approve_or_deny_bills acts on.

output.description: The bills pending the session user's approval.

approve_or_deny_bills.title: Approve or deny bills
approve_or_deny_bills.description: Record an approval decision on one or more bills. Approving is what makes a bill payable; denying stops it. Each entry is {"billId": ..., "action": ..., "comment": ...} and the decision is logged against your user.

decisions.description: The decisions to record, each {"billId": "00n...", "action": <approve or deny>, optionally "comment": <reason>}.

list_bill_approval_policies.title: List bill approval policies
list_bill_approval_policies.description: Read the rules deciding who must approve which bills -- by amount, vendor or accounting dimension.

page.description: Page cursor from a previous response.

list_payments.title: List payments
list_payments.description: Read the payments you have made, with their status, process date and the bills each covered. `filters` narrows by vendor, status or date.

page.description: Page cursor from a previous response.

get_payment.title: Get a payment
get_payment.description: Read one payment -- amount, funding account, status and which bills it settled.

create_payment.title: Pay a bill
create_payment.description: Send a real payment to a vendor. Money leaves the named funding account on `process_date`; the vendor is paid by whatever method the funding account and their payment options imply. This is not bookkeeping -- use record_ap_payment for a payment you already made elsewhere. Once processing has begun it can only be voided, not edited.

funding_account.description: Where the money comes from -- {"type": <account type>, "id": <bank or card account id>}. list_bank_accounts and list_card_accounts give the ids.

processing_options.description: How BILL should process it -- {"createBill": false} to pay an existing bill rather than creating one, plus options such as {"requestPayFaster": true}.

vendor_id.description: The vendor being paid. Required unless `bill_id` implies them.

process_date.description: Date BILL should take the money, as YYYY-MM-DD.

description.description: Description carried on the payment, and printed on a cheque.

transaction_number.description: Your own reference for this payment.

output.description: The created payment, with its status.

record_ap_payment.title: Record a payment made outside BILL
record_ap_payment.description: Mark bills as paid without moving any money -- for a cheque you wrote or a transfer you made yourself. `payments` lists which bills were settled and for how much. Bookkeeping only: nothing is sent to the vendor.

process_date.description: Date the payment was made, as YYYY-MM-DD.

to_print_check.description: Whether the payment should be marked as a cheque to print.

payments.description: Which bills were settled, each {"billId": "00n...", "amount": ..., optionally "vendorCredits": [...]}.

sync_reference.description: The payment's reference in your accounting system.

allow_export.description: Allow the recorded payment to sync to your accounting system.

cancel_payment.title: Cancel a payment
cancel_payment.description: Cancel a payment BILL has not yet processed. Once it is in flight this fails and void_payment is the only route -- so cancel early.

void_payment.title: Void a payment
void_payment.description: Void a payment that has already been processed -- a cheque gone astray, a duplicate. `type` says what kind of void, `reason` why, and both are kept on the record. Cancelling is the cheaper option while it is still possible.

type.description: The kind of void, as BILL's void types define it.

reason.description: Why the payment is being voided; kept on the record.

get_exchange_rate.title: Get BILL's exchange rate
get_exchange_rate.description: Read the rate BILL would use to pay one vendor a given amount, which is what an international payment will actually cost. Both the vendor and the amount are required, since the rate depends on them.

vendor_id.description: The vendor being paid, by their `009...` id.

amount.description: The amount to be paid, in the vendor's bill currency.

list_vendor_credits.title: List vendor credits
list_vendor_credits.description: Read the credits vendors owe you -- returns, overpayments -- which can be applied against bills when paying.

page.description: Page cursor from a previous response.

create_vendor_credit.title: Create a vendor credit
create_vendor_credit.description: Record a credit a vendor has given you, which can then be applied to bills through `vendor_credits` when creating a bill or a payment.

credit_date.description: Date of the credit, as YYYY-MM-DD.

reference_number.description: The vendor's reference for the credit.

list_recurring_bills.title: List recurring bills
list_recurring_bills.description: Read the templates BILL uses to generate bills on a schedule -- rent, subscriptions -- with their intervals.

page.description: Page cursor from a previous response.

list_customers.title: List customers
list_customers.description: Read the organization's customers -- the people you invoice. Ids come back prefixed with `0cu`.

page.description: Page cursor from a previous response.

get_customer.title: Get a customer
get_customer.description: Read one customer by their `0cu...` id -- contact details, addresses and terms.

customer_id.description: The customer's id, which begins with `0cu`.

create_customer.title: Create a customer
create_customer.description: Create a customer you can invoice. Name and email are required -- the email is where invoices and payment links are sent.

company_name.description: Their company name, when different from `name`.

account_number.description: Your account number for them, printed on invoices.

payment_term_id.description: Payment term id, which sets invoice due dates.

invoice_currency.description: Currency their invoices are denominated in.

output.description: The created customer, with its `0cu...` id.

update_customer.title: Update a customer
update_customer.description: Change a customer's details. Only the fields you send are touched.

archive_customer.title: Archive a customer
archive_customer.description: Archive a customer so they cannot be chosen on new invoices. Their history stays and restore_customer undoes it.

restore_customer.title: Restore an archived customer
restore_customer.description: Bring an archived customer back into use on new invoices.

list_invoices.title: List invoices
list_invoices.description: Read the invoices you have issued, with their status and balance. `filters` is how you get the aged-debt view -- unpaid invoices, or one customer's. Ids come back prefixed with `00e`.

page.description: Page cursor from a previous response.

get_invoice.title: Get an invoice
get_invoice.description: Read one invoice by its `00e...` id -- customer, line items, totals and how much is still outstanding.

invoice_id.description: The invoice's id, which begins with `00e`.

create_invoice.title: Create an invoice
create_invoice.description: Invoice a customer. `customer` identifies them -- by `id`, or by name and email to create them on the fly -- and `invoice_line_items` carries the lines, each needing a quantity. Setting `processing_options` to {"sendEmail": true} emails the customer immediately; otherwise use send_invoice when you are ready.

customer.description: Who to invoice -- {"id": "0cu..."} for an existing customer, or {"name": ..., "email": ...} to create one.

line_items.description: The invoice lines, each {"quantity": ..., "price": ..., "description": ..., optionally "taxable" and "classifications"}.

invoice_number.description: Your invoice number. BILL assigns one when omitted.

due_date.description: When payment is due, as YYYY-MM-DD.

payment_term_id.description: Payment term id, which sets the due date when it is not given.

pay_to_chart_of_account_id.description: Chart of accounts id the receipt should be booked against.

processing_options.description: Options such as {"sendEmail": true} to email the customer at once.

credit_amount.description: Credit to apply against the invoice.

sales_tax_item_id.description: Sales tax item id to apply to taxable lines.

enable_card_payment.description: Let the customer pay this invoice by card.

output.description: The created invoice, with its `00e...` id.

update_invoice.title: Update an invoice
update_invoice.description: Change an invoice. As with bills, line items are addressed by their own ids and anything omitted is removed -- read the invoice first.

line_items.description: The invoice's lines after the update, each with its `id`.

send_invoice.title: Email an invoice to the customer
send_invoice.description: Send an invoice to the customer by email. `reply_to.userId` is the BILL user it appears to come from and `recipient.to` the addresses. This reaches a real inbox and cannot be recalled.

reply_to.description: Who the email comes from -- {"userId": <BILL user id>}.

output.description: Confirmation that the invoice was sent.

get_invoice_payment_link.title: Get an invoice payment link
get_invoice_payment_link.description: Create a link the customer can use to pay an invoice themselves. `email` is the recipient the link is issued for, and `return_url` where they land afterwards.

customer_id.description: The customer the link is for, by their `0cu...` id.

email.description: Recipient email address the link is issued for.

return_url.description: Where to send the customer once payment is complete.

charge_customer.title: Charge a customer
charge_customer.description: Take payment from a customer's stored bank account or card. Real money moves and the customer's authorization must already be on file -- set it with authorize_customer_charge. Not reversible through this API.

invoices.description: Which invoices the charge settles, each {"id": "00e...", "amount": ...}.

customer_bank_account_id.description: Which stored bank account to debit, from list_customer_bank_accounts.

process_date.description: Date to take the money, as YYYY-MM-DD.

record_ar_payment.title: Record a payment a customer made outside BILL
record_ar_payment.description: Mark invoices as paid without taking any money -- for a cheque or transfer you received directly. Bookkeeping only; nothing is charged.

payment_date.description: Date the money arrived, as YYYY-MM-DD.

payment_type.description: How they paid, as BILL's payment types define it.

list_received_payments.title: List received payments
list_received_payments.description: Read the payments customers have made, with which invoices each settled -- the receivable side of the ledger.

page.description: Page cursor from a previous response.

archive_invoice.title: Archive an invoice
archive_invoice.description: Archive an invoice so it leaves the receivable list. Payments already recorded against it are unaffected; restore_invoice undoes this.

restore_invoice.title: Restore an archived invoice
restore_invoice.description: Bring an archived invoice back into the receivable list.

list_credit_memos.title: List credit memos
list_credit_memos.description: Read the credit memos issued to customers -- credits that can be applied against their invoices.

page.description: Page cursor from a previous response.

list_customer_bank_accounts.title: List a customer's bank accounts
list_customer_bank_accounts.description: Read the bank accounts stored for one customer, whose ids charge_customer debits. Masked, as the API returns them.

page.description: Page cursor from a previous response.

output.description: A page of the customer's bank accounts.

authorize_customer_charge.title: Set a customer's charge authorization
authorize_customer_charge.description: Record that a customer has authorised you to debit their account, which is the precondition for charge_customer. A legal record, not a formality.

is_authorized.description: Whether the customer has authorised being charged.

list_bank_accounts.title: List bank accounts
list_bank_accounts.description: Read the organization's bank accounts -- the funding accounts payments are drawn from. An account's id is what a payment's `funding_account` names.

page.description: Page cursor from a previous response.

get_bank_account.title: Get a bank account
get_bank_account.description: Read one bank account -- its name, masked number and verification status. An unverified account cannot fund payments.

list_card_accounts.title: List card accounts
list_card_accounts.description: Read the organization's card accounts, which can fund payments where the vendor accepts card. `card_user_status` is required -- it selects the accounts whose card user is in that state.

card_user_status.description: Which card users to include, as BILL's card user statuses define them -- required by the endpoint.

list_chart_of_accounts.title: List the chart of accounts
list_chart_of_accounts.description: Read the organization's chart of accounts. These ids are what a bill's or invoice's `classifications.chartOfAccountId` refers to, so this is the lookup before coding anything.

page.description: Page cursor from a previous response.

create_chart_of_account.title: Create a chart of accounts entry
create_chart_of_account.description: Add an account to the chart of accounts. `account_type` and `account_number` should match your accounting system, since BILL syncs against it.

account_number.description: The account number in your accounting system.

account_type.description: The account type, as BILL's account types define it.

parent_id.description: Parent account id, for a nested account.

list_departments.title: List departments
list_departments.description: Read the organization's departments, whose ids a bill's or invoice's `classifications.departmentId` refers to.

page.description: Page cursor from a previous response.

list_items.title: List items
list_items.description: Read the organization's items -- the products and services invoice and bill lines can reference by `itemId`.

page.description: Page cursor from a previous response.

list_accounting_classes.title: List accounting classes
list_accounting_classes.description: Read the organization's accounting classes, whose ids `classifications.accountingClassId` refers to.

page.description: Page cursor from a previous response.

list_employees.title: List employees
list_employees.description: Read the employee records BILL holds for classification purposes -- used to attribute bills and expenses to a person.

page.description: Page cursor from a previous response.

list_bill_documents.title: List a bill's documents
list_bill_documents.description: Read the documents attached to a bill -- the scanned invoice, receipts -- with their ids and upload status.

page.description: Page cursor from a previous response.

output.description: A page of the bill's documents.

get_attachment.title: Get an attachment
get_attachment.description: Read one attachment's details -- name, type and size -- by its id, for any object it hangs off.

delete_attachment.title: Delete an attachment
delete_attachment.description: Delete an attachment from whatever it was attached to. The file goes and cannot be recovered -- which matters when it is the only copy of a vendor invoice.

output.description: Confirmation that the attachment was deleted.

search_network.title: Search the BILL network
search_network.description: Find another organization on the BILL network by name -- the first step in connecting to a vendor or customer who also uses BILL, after which payments between you settle electronically. Narrow an ambiguous name with their postcode or the account number they gave you.

name.description: Organization name to search the network for.

scope.description: Which side of the network to search, as BILL's scopes define it.

zip_or_postal_code.description: Their postcode, to disambiguate a common name.

account_number.description: The account number they gave you, which matches them exactly.

invite_vendor_to_network.title: Send a vendor a connection request
invite_vendor_to_network.description: Ask a vendor on the BILL network to connect with you. They see and must accept the request, so this is outward-facing -- and once accepted, payments to them settle electronically.

vendor_id.description: Your vendor record for them, by its `009...` id.

invite_customer_to_network.title: Send a customer a connection request
invite_customer_to_network.description: Ask a customer on the BILL network to connect, so their payments to you settle electronically. They must accept it.

customer_id.description: Your customer record for them, by its `0cu...` id.
